title: Dynamic escalation profiles and runbook templates
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce dynamic escalation profiles and variable-driven runbook templates. Provides safe defaults and canary rollout. No breaking changes.
description:
Context: On-call teams need flexible escalation policies that adapt to responder load and alert storm conditions. This PR introduces two features in the slo-toolkit: 1) dynamic escalation profiles — evaluable policies that adjust escalation timing and routing based on runtime signals (alert rate, average ack latency, oncall headcount); and 2) templated runbooks — parameterized YAML templates that incident-bot and on-call tooling can instantiate with live context.

Motivation: customers have asked for automatic hold-windows and progressive escalation that reduce noise during large-scale maintenance or cascading failures (ENG-2143). This change aims to reduce false escalations, speed up human response for high-severity incidents, and make runbooks reusable across teams.

What changed (high level):
- Add a new evaluation engine (slo-toolkit/policies/profile_engine.go) that evaluates profile rules against telemetry and responder load.
- Add runbook template files under templates/runbooks/*.yaml and a templating utility (slo-toolkit/templates/renderer.go) that supports variable interpolation, conditional steps, and preflight checks.
- Integrate with incident-bot by adding a lightweight HTTP hook (cli/escalate.go) that exports a preview endpoint for instantiated runbooks and suggested escalation adjustments.
- Add a CLI command `sloctl profile simulate` to run a deterministic simulation against historical alert traces for validation.
- Add unit and integration tests plus an e2e harness that runs a short alert storm simulation.

Checklist:
- [x] Add profile engine and tests
- [x] Add runbook template renderer and sample templates
- [x] Add CLI simulate command and docs
- [x] Add incident-bot hook and wiring
- [x] Add canary rollout (50% teams) config
- [x] Documentation and example templates in docs/runbooks.md

- feat(template): runbook templating and renderer
- feat(cli): add profile simulate command and integration
- fix(ci): mock telemetry sources for deterministic tests
- chore(docs): runbook examples and usage guide
- perf(profile): small optimization for evaluation hot path

Changed files (high level):
- src/profile_engine.go
- src/templates/renderer.go
- templates/runbooks/standard_incident.yaml
- cli/escalate.go
- cli/simulate_cmd.go

- docs/runbooks.md
- Makefile (new targets for simulate)
- integration/testdata/sample_trace.json

Review conversation: Reviewer Omar: "Nice incremental design. Two asks: (1) we need metrics for headroom so teams can see how often a profile is suppressing escalations, and (2) make the default hold-window conservative in prod. Also, add a short migration note for teams that currently use static policies." Author (Maya): "Thanks — added headroom metrics (slo_toolkit.profile.suppressed_count and .effective_hold_ms), tightened defaults to conservative values, and added migration docs in docs/runbooks.md. The simulate CLI can produce a comparison report to help migration." Reviewer Priya: "Can we add a small e2e test that runs an alert burst through incident-bot to exercise the hook?" Author: "Added tests/e2e/simulated_storm_test.go which exercises the hook against a local stub of incident-bot; flakiness noted in first CI run but fixed by deterministic timestamps."

CI summary:
- CircleCI: unit tests initially failed on mocks (flaky), rerun -> all unit tests pass
- Integration: e2e harness passes in 2/3 workers initially; fixed timeout and reran to green
- Lint/format: pass

Merge outcome: merged via squash.

Canary rollout: feature gate defaulted to false; deploy pipeline will flip to 50% of teams for 48 hours before global rollout.

Backfill/upgrade notes:
- No DB migrations.
- Teams using static policies can migrate by running `sloctl profile convert` which generates a best-effort dynamic profile and a simulation report.

Related: ENG-2143, PM-98, docs/runbooks.md
